speech_en: Bubbles first — the thread gets spun outside!
speech_de: Erst Bläschen — den Faden spinnt die Maschine draußen!
scenario: A big round cheerful cartoon cell character, far too big for the frame, carrying five or six plain round secretory bubbles inside its body and tipping more of them out of a small doorway into a chunky smiling spinning machine at the lower right; a single broad ribbon-like strand leaves the machine's nozzle only, running diagonally down and off the bottom-right corner. This is the subject's scientific trap made visual: inside the cell there is no thread at all, only protein-filled vesicles — the fibre exists only after secretion and spinning, outside the cell. The strand is a single diagonal ribbon leaving the frame, never a hub with lines radiating from it (the unrecoverable starburst failure), and there is no spider, no web and no goat anywhere.
status: DONE. The monthly Gemini spending cap that blocked the original 2026-08 attempt has been lifted; rendered on 2026-09-06 with gemini-2.5-flash-image in ONE API call (attempt 1, no re-roll, no model escalation). The saved 2026-08 prompt was refined first rather than used verbatim: (a) it banned every thread everywhere, which throws away the subject's actual teaching point — the new prompt keeps bubbles-only inside the cell and puts one strand after a spinning machine, matching the kids' description ('It comes out as a gooey protein, not thread — turning it into an actual fibre is a separate job for a spinning machine later'); (b) the ALL-CAPS noun 'CELL character' was lower-cased and 'writing of any kind' explicitly forbidden, because that exact capitalisation baked the literal word CELL into lentiviral-vector attempt 1; (c) the composition was aimed diagonally so the character is sliced by the top and left edges and the strand leaves through the bottom-right corner. Attempt 1 came back frame-free, text-free and starburst-free, but left a white margin down the right side, so per SKILL.md's crop-don't-re-roll rule the raw PNG was cropped to box (0,144,880,1024) and re-traced through coloring.py's own to_bitmap/trace_paths/build_svg — no extra API call. Crop box chosen by measuring 51 candidate crops on the COMPOSED page, not on the raster. Final composed .coloring.svg rasterised with cairosvg at 500px, ink fraction in the outermost rows/cols of the top 72% of the page (the atlas-wide convention): top 0.0000 (structural — the speech bubble owns the top of the frame on all ~120 pages), bottom 0.0960, left 0.0472, right 0.0648, overall ink 0.0920. Three-edge bleed, all three inside the healthy 0.02-0.27 band. No frame (densest outer 8-row/col band peaks at 0.078, nowhere near a solid border), no baked text, no starburst, no spider, no web, no goat. Both #labels-en and #labels-de layers present with real em dashes and real umlauts (Bläschen, draußen).

prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080.

THIS IS A MACRO CLOSE-UP SHOT, LIKE A ZOOMED-IN PHONE CAMERA PHOTO TAKEN TOO CLOSE. The subject is so close to the "camera" that it does NOT fully fit in the frame: the top of the big round character is CUT OFF by the TOP edge, its rounded left side is CUT OFF by the LEFT edge, the little machine on the right is CUT OFF by the RIGHT edge, and the strand leaving the machine runs off the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner. There must be ZERO empty white background space visible anywhere in the image — every part of the 1080x1080 canvas is covered by either black line-art or white space that belongs INSIDE a drawn shape. If you can see plain empty background at any edge, the drawing is WRONG — redo it bigger and closer.

SCENE (draw it oversized, then let the frame crop it): A big round cheerful cartoon character shaped like a blob-shaped body cell — a huge soft round body with a smaller round smiling face drawn inside it near the middle (two dot eyes, a big happy smile), like a friendly cell with a nucleus face. It fills the left two thirds of the picture and is far too big for the frame, so its top and its left side are sliced off by the edges. Floating inside its body, around the little face, are five or six plain round bubbles of different sizes, each a simple closed circle with plenty of white space inside for colouring — some with one short curved highlight line inside. The bubbles are separate, unconnected, never touching each other, never stretched, never joined by any line.

On the lower right of the picture, tilted diagonally, sits a chunky cheerful little machine with a wide funnel mouth on top, a rounded body, one round crank handle on its side and a single round nozzle at its lower right corner; the machine is smiling with a simple curved line and is so big that its right side is sliced off by the RIGHT edge and its base is sliced off by the BOTTOM edge. The big round character is tipping three or four of the same plain round bubbles out of a small rounded doorway on its lower-right side; the bubbles drop in a gentle diagonal line into the machine's funnel mouth.

Out of the machine's nozzle, and only from there, comes ONE single smooth strand: draw it as a broad flat ribbon with two bold parallel outlines and open white space between them, gently wavy, thick enough to colour inside, running diagonally down and to the right and sliced off by the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner of the picture. Exactly one strand, going in exactly one direction, with no branches, no loops, no net, no criss-cross, and nothing else attached to it. Keep the rest of the background bare apart from two or three simple rounded confetti dots near the funnel.

STYLE — coloring book line art: BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed. NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black fills anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only). Simple, cheerful, chunky shapes with open white space INSIDE each shape for colouring.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN:
- Any visible empty white background, wall, sky or margin space — the artwork must be so zoomed-in and oversized that it touches or crosses the left, right and bottom edges, with elements literally cut off by the edges.
- ANY strand, thread, string, fibre, line or trail INSIDE the big round character or leaving the big round character — everything inside its body and everything coming out of its doorway is plain round separate bubbles only. The single strand exists ONLY after the machine's nozzle.
- ANY spider, spider legs, spider eyes, cobweb, spiderweb, net or mesh pattern anywhere.
- ANY starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, halo of rays, or several lines fanning out from one point anywhere.
- ANY rectangle, box outline, picture frame, panel edge, border line or vignette around the whole picture.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures, watermarks or writing of any kind anywhere in the image.
- NO speech bubble or thought bubble (added separately afterwards).
- NO goat, no animal body, no udder, no human figure and no human face anywhere.
- NO fighting, no scary imagery, no sad or worried character.
